title: Micro-onboard sprint manifest (90m) - draft
content:
Purpose and scope:

A compact, repeatable 90-minute in-person or virtual sprint designed to get a new integrator (engineer or solutions engineer) from zero to an instrumented Hello World that calls the Redwood API, validates a basic telemetry contract, and wires a fallback policy. This is intentionally opinionated: small surface area, strong defaults, explicit gates for handing off to full integration work.

Audience:
- Primary: backend/frontend engineers, solutions engineers doing customer demos
- Secondary: docs writers, QA engineers who will maintain smoke tests

Goals (measurable):
- Local dev environment ready in 15 minutes
- First successful API call in 25 minutes
- Telemetry ping + token-level breakdown visible in Console within 60 minutes
- Canary fallback wired and tested before end of session

Prerequisites (ask participants to complete before sprint):
- GitHub account + GH access for repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-hello-world
- Docker installed (optional but recommended)
- Node 18+, Python 3.10+, or Go 1.20 installed locally
- Sandbox API key (redwood_sbox_... ) provisioned and emailed to attendees

90-minute timeline (timeboxes):
- 0–10m: quick orientation + goals + environment checklist
- 10–25m: local install and run the minimal Hello World (Node or Python path)
- 25–45m: add a prompt template & structured output parsing; assert stable output shape
- 45–60m: connect to Console: verify telemetry + token breakdown; fix any sampling gaps
- 60–75m: implement fallback policy (model variant and quiet degraded response) and simulate upstream errors
- 75–85m: run smoke tests + record demo script
- 85–90m: retro + next steps (owner for follow-up tasks)

Environment matrix (default recommended):
- Node template: npm init -y; npm i @redwood/inference@latest; run node quickstart.js
- Python template: python -m venv venv; source venv/bin/activate; pip install redwood-inference-sdk; python quickstart.py
- Go template: go mod init hello-redwood; go get github.com/redwood-inference/sdk; go run main.go

Minimal Hello World snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- Node (quickstart.js):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
  async function main(){
    const r = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood/fast-v1', prompt: 'Write a two-line haiku about code.' });
    console.log(r.text);
  }
  main();

- Python (quickstart.py):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_KEY'))
  resp = c.generate(model='redwood/fast-v1', prompt='Two-line haiku about code')
  print(resp.text)

Expected smoke output (success):
- "haiku": string with two short lines
- HTTP 200 with body: {"id":..., "text": "..."} (we treat shape, not exact content)

Telemetry contract (minimal, required for handoff):
- Every user-visible request must emit an event with keys: event_name (string), sdk_lang (string), model (string), token_count (int), latency_ms (int), sample_id (string).
- For this sprint we assert the presence of event_name="sdk.request" and token_count > 0 in Console for at least one call.
- Questions: do we want SDK-level user_id vs app-provided user_id for the first pass? (TBD)

Gating criteria to mark the quickstart as complete for a customer trial:
- SDK call succeeds locally against Sandbox API key
- Telemetry event appears in Console within 10 minutes of call
- Fallback policy triggers when simulating 503 from primary model
- README updated with any environment quirks discovered during session

Failure modes & quick fixes (pair-programmer tips):
- 401/403: check REDWOOD_KEY, ensure sandbox key hasn't expired, check region restrictions
- 429: reduce batch size, use smaller model or switch to redwood/fast-v1
- Empty response / partial tokens: try streaming enabled client; ensure prompt ends with newline; verify seq length limits
- Telemetry not showing: confirm SDK version supports telemetry opt-in, check sampling rate env var REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_SAMPLING=1 for sandbox

Quality checks (mini smoke tests to commit):
- test/hello.test.js: hit generate endpoint and assert status 200 and text length > 10
- test/telemetry.test.py: call generate and poll Console API for recent events containing sample_id returned by SDK

Handoff checklist (what to add to customer repo when sprint ends):
- Add .env.example with REDWOOD_KEY placeholder
- Add quickstart scripts for Node/Python/Go to package.json / Makefile
- Create a tiny CI job (github actions) that runs hello smoke test on PRs; gate merges on test pass
- Link to customer Confluence page and add owner for follow-up integration work

Open design notes and low-priority ideas (brainstorm fragments):
- Could we add a one-click CloudSandbox link that injects API key into a temporary environment for attendees? Pros: removes env hurdle. Cons: security implications and rotation complexity.
- A tiny web demo (React) that streams tokens and shows per-token cost meter would be great for SEs. Low-priority prototype.
- Consider a "mini-telemetry inspector" CLI that fetches the last N events for a sample_id to avoid flipping to Console UI during demos.

Session artifacts to create after pilot run:
- PR: add quickstart CI job and increment SDK sample to stable 1.0.2
- Docs: short single-page quickstart with 5 commands and 3 screenshots (Console token map, fallback trace, smoke test passing)
- Follow-up ticket: integrate sampling opt-in into the SDK so sandbox users default to visible telemetry during onboarding sessions

Notes to self (Ava):
- Run this once with SE team before shipping as \"official\" kit. Capture timing deviations and common confusion points.
- Validate the telemetry contract against Console team API (CONFLUENCE-1234).
- Add a tiny badge in README showing \"plays well in 90 minutes\" and link to one-click calendar invite template for workshops.

Unresolved questions to raise in next sync:
- How visible should model variant fallbacks be in Console by default?
- Do we want to recommend a different default model for memory-constrained mobile demos?

References and local links (for pilot):
- GitHub seed repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-hello-world
- Telemetry design doc: CONFLUENCE-1234
- Follow-up PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-hello-world/pull/67

End of draft. This is intentionally terse and pragmatic; will expand into the canonical quickstart page after 1 pilot run.
